stem: Alok has a square of side $4\,\mathrm{cm}$. He makes a new square whose side is $12\,\mathrm{cm}$, so the side length is multiplied by $3$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states how the area changes from the first square to the new square?

options.text: The area of the new square is three times the area of the first square because the side length was multiplied by $3$.
The area of the new square is nine times the area of the first square because the side length was multiplied by $3$.
The areas are equal because both shapes are squares.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Area of a square is side squared. Multiplying the side by 3 multiplies the area by 3²=9; first area 16 cm² becomes 144 cm².

teacher.key_rationale: For side s, area is s². Scaling side by k scales area by k². Here k=3 so area factor is 9.
